newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch swine fever spreads, Poland bans pig imports.
newsitem.headline: Dutch swine fever spreads, Poland bans pig imports.

text.p: The Dutch Agriculture Ministry said on Friday it had detected two new cases of swine fever, taking the number of affected farms to four, and confirmed that Poland had banned the import of pigs from the Netherlands.
"There have been two new cases of swine fever and Poland has closed its border to Dutch pigs, porkmeat and pig products," a ministry spokeswoman told Reuters.

According to Dutch news agency ANP, Polish imports of pork products in the first nine months of last year amounted to 2,300 tonnes, a tiny fraction of the 560,000 tonnes exported by the Netherlands during the period.

The two newly infected farms, which have been closed off like the others, are near the first two and within an area towards the south of the Netherlands that was designated by the farm ministry on Thursday and where all pigs will have to be slaughtered.
There would be no new measures as a result of Friday's discovery, the spokeswoman said.

The first outbreak of swine fever in the Netherlands since 1992 was discovered this week on Tuesday at a farm in the province of North Brabant, with the second reported on Thursday at another farm 1.5 kilometres away.
The spokeswoman also confirmed that Belgium had tightened regulations over the import of Dutch pigs but not halted them.
"The Belgian authorities are asking for extra paperwork but you can still export pigs to Belgium," she said.

On Thursday, the ministry said it would order the destruction of all pigs within a two kilometre radius of the first two swine fever cases, a measure which could involve the slaughter of between 20,000 and 30,000 pigs.

The transport of all animals, apart from poultry, would be banned within a 12 kilometre radius of the two farms in a move that exceeded EU disease management regulations calling for a 10 kilometre transport embargo, a spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"We're still carrying out blood tests in the area. This is a very dangerous disease and it can spread very quickly, but we're hoping it has been contained," she said.

Germany earlier this week prohibited the export of pigs for slaughter from four German states after an outbreak of swine fever. Authorities have ordered the slaughter of over 14,000 pigs to contain it but Belgium and Switzerland have announced restrictions on German imports of live pigs and pork meat.
The U.S. Agriculture Department said on Wednesday it was monitoring the Dutch outbreak but would not impose any trade restrictions yet. -- David Evans, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
